qt: to the Commission Emmanouil Fragkos (ECR) Subject:

Regulation (EC) No 1099/2009 introduces the requirement for compulsory stunning prior to slaughter, whilst allowing for a derogation in the case of religious rites. This exemption raises serious animal welfare issues. The Court of Justice of the EU, in its judgment C-336/19, recognised the possibility for Member States to impose reversible stunning obligations also on religious slaughter. At the same time, questions remain about the import and circulation of products from animals slaughtered without stunning and about the information provided to European consumers. In view of the above, can the Commission say: 1.

Does it intend to propose ending the derogation set out in Article 4(4) of Regulation 1099/2009, thereby making prior stunning mandatory for all commercial slaughter within the EU, regardless of religious rites?

Will it consider banning the import, trade and placing on the EU market of meat from animals slaughtered without prior stunning, as well as mandatory labelling of slaughter methods and enhanced traceability?

In its view, would a general ban on the production, trade, sale and consumption of certified halal products be compatible with the principle of proportionality and the Charter of Fundamental Rights? If not, what specific legal obstacles can it identify and what additional animal protection measures does it intend to propose?
